task_instance: Create a new Expo (blank-typescript) app, set bundleIdentifier/appleTeamId, add an iOS App Clip target with `create-target clip` (the underlying tool of `bun create target clip`), wire the Associated Domains entitlements for both parent and clip targets, run `expo prebuild -p ios` to generate the native Xcode project, verify the App Clip target and its derived bundle ID/entitlements exist in the generated project, and author the apple-app-site-association (AASA) JSON file with an `appclips` block.
evidence: Created app at may20/ via `bunx create-expo-app@latest may20 --template blank-typescript`. Set bundleIdentifier=com.example.may20, appleTeamId=XX57RJ5UTD, and associatedDomains (applinks/appclips) in app.json. `bun create target clip` itself failed with 'HTTP Proxy Network Error: Forbidden' because it shells out to `npx expo install` which pings api.expo.dev (blocked by the sandbox's outbound proxy policy, confirmed via `curl $HTTPS_PROXY/__agentproxy/status` showing 403 connect_rejected entries for api.expo.dev/cdp.expo.dev/reactnative.directory). Worked around by installing the dependency directly with `bun add @bacons/apple-targets` (registry.npmjs.org is proxy-allowlisted) and then running the underlying `bunx create-target clip` binary directly, which succeeded, wrote targets/clip/{expo-target.config.js,Info.plist,AppDelegate.swift,...}, and added the plugin to app.json. Edited targets/clip/expo-target.config.js to add the appclips associated-domains entitlement. Ran `npx expo prebuild -p ios --no-install`, which succeeded (only a non-fatal icon-download warning due to github.com being blocked). Verified generated ios/ project: `grep PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER ios/*.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj` shows both com.example.may20 and com.example.may20.clip targets; ios/.targets/clip/generated.entitlements contains the appclips associated-domains entry and parent-application-identifiers; ios/may20/may20.entitlements contains both applinks and appclips entries. Also authored and JSON-validated public/.well-known/apple-app-site-association with applinks/appclips/webcredentials blocks per the skill's step 5. This covers the skill's core, open-source deliverable (adding and correctly configuring an App Clip target in an Expo project). Steps requiring an actual Apple Developer account (`bunx setup-safari` to register bundle IDs / create App Store Connect entries), EAS/TestFlight build+submit, and live HTTPS hosting of the AASA file were not attempted since they require paid Apple Developer Program membership and account credentials, consistent with the skill doc's own stated requirements ('Shipping one requires an Apple Developer Program membership and App Store review') and the sandbox's no-credentials/no-paid-services rule.
